body:
PROTOCOL.md said one second provider's shape and only one; this makes the rule what it had become already -- a shape per provider, each in a folder. `src/provider/gemini` mirrors `src/provider/anthropic`: `wire.h` keeps plain types for the modules, `wire.cpp` keeps Agora's `GeminiStreamRouter` and its JSON behind them, and a payload of one frame goes in whole.

What the wire then says, in its own words: `src/provider.cc` gains the fourth wire -- the family asked before the base's own /v1beta suffix (which would otherwise read Google as OpenAI), the method carrying the model and asking `alt=sse`, `x-goog-api-key` for the key, and `gemini_body_of` writing turns as contents of parts, what is told as a `systemInstruction`, the five choices under one `generationConfig` with thinking as its `thinkingBudget` (thousands when asked for, zero when not -- this wire thinks on by itself otherwise), tools as `functionDeclarations`, and a call answered by `functionResponse` against the name it went out under, looked up from the turns. `src/provider/stream.cc` takes the third shape into the same queue as the other two, so nothing reading an answer can tell which it arrived in.

The offered list gains `gemini-2.5-flash` as a seventh answerer (family `gemini`), PROTOCOL.md's bullet follows the folder, and `test/provider_gemini_test.cc` reads three things back: an answer's SSE whole (thought, text, a call with no invented id, usage, a normalized stop), a failure the wire reports inside the stream, and the body part by part -- contents, instruction, config, thinking budget, declarations.
title: the gemini wire read through a folder of its own
